doc.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996

title: Milt Hinton's health and character
summary: He praises Milt Hinton's kindness and generosity and talks about his ill health and recovery.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: George was kind of a protégé of Milt, wasn’t he?
Well Milt is still this way, he’s still the Daddy of them all. He’s physically not well, he’s got some problems, I understand he’s getting — Sharon, how old is Milt now? SR: 86 or 87.

Yeah, 86 or 87. His wife’s not too well. She has got some problems, but they are the nicest people, and I can’t think of one nasty or even off thing about Milt, ever. He’s always been a gentleman to everybody, kind, generous to a fault. I can go by asking myself, if I called him and said, “Milt you’ve got to do this thing for me because I need you for such-and-such like that, and I can’t pay you anything,” he’d say okay. Fortunately it didn’t happen very often, but, and he would take off from someplace else to do this, because we were friends.

Well you can measure I think how they’re, Milt and Mona are looked upon by when you see them at a festival or something, they can’t even get down the hall because so many people just want to be around them.
They are good people. They really are good people. All over the world he’s known. Somebody told me that he’s getting better.
I’m happy to say. We call every once in a while, you know call them up, and Milt, he wants to play. Physically I don’t think he has the energy yet. He may have now, who knows?
